findings.title: Active flow needs a bounded await and this witness
findings.evidence: Plan line 31 restricts eligible expression/return/assignment shapes to call/new and Name-position symbols. UnifiedAgent lines 44/48 are return await, 64/97 assign await this.provider calls, and 71-74 assign await this.toolRegistry.execute over four lines. Installed TypeScriptLexer emits Keyword for await/this and Name.Other for the qualified members. A literal whitelist can accept the logger or getToolDefinitions and still exclude the actual dispatch.
findings.change: Specify an optional await at the operand and optional keyword this as receiver in those narrow existing shapes. Define the symbol string, final Name position, multiline completion and 8-visible-line bound. Use unrelated async qualified and multiline positives plus comment/log/string/unfinished/out-of-view negatives. Check the exact projected active donor and archived Python executor span without adding source-specific production rules. Compact numbered [line,text] JSON for the entire local TS body fits the four-source allowance (5425 characters including object fields).

findings.title: Report validation is atomic per invocation only
findings.evidence: Plan lines 44/51 promise failure before write and no effects for rejected support. _CapabilityTool.execute catches report errors and records a failed ToolResult. NativeReAct.run (agents/native_react.py lines 352-358) appends the observation and keeps generating. WorkService checks failures only when the runner returns. A validly encoded bad span followed by a valid payload can therefore write a real file before the first failure is surfaced. A wire-envelope checker alone accepts both envelopes.
findings.change: Define request-local handling of the first rejected support and distinguish failed-invocation atomicity from runner-wide no-write. To promise whole-request no-write for a rejected span, stop before the next generation/dispatch using trusted current-bound failure state. Preserve the SDK loop and every original failed event. Script a bad span followed by a would-be valid write and assert exact dispatch count, file presence and CLI2. Separately test committed write followed by malformed final as needs_attention with original bytes/IDs. Never waive an earlier fatal tool failure.

findings.title: Capture possible writes even when result is late or unsuccessful
findings.evidence: SDK tools/_stubs.py lines 389-421 time out a worker future and cannot cancel active execution. FileWriteTool can return an error after opening/truncating a file. _WorkFileTool.execute records its result at return, and WorkService derives needs_attention from successful writes or may_have_committed. Only the window adapter currently marks a possible effect. A compose timeout/error before a success record can therefore be classified failed with no recorded possible file effect.
findings.change: Define the request-bound write-attempt boundary after complete report validation and path checks, before nested SDK file mutation; preserve path/identity and uncertainty without inventing a successful write. Handle outer timeout racing the worker, including before the marker is observed, by fencing late writes or classifying the in-flight attempt as possible. Script a partial-write error and an already-running delayed SDK writer; verify needs_attention, no replay, fresh independent readback when available, and no cross-request attribution. Keep all unsupported spans rejected before entering the mutation boundary.

nonblocking: The borrowed view is feasible on this installed SDK. The owner initializes once under the ask lock. Jarvis has explicit close/context-manager teardown and no destructor; dropping an unclosed shallow view leaves the owner alive. Keep shared bus, policy and rate limiter, never use the view as a context manager. _run_agent still constructs tools and wires security with the original identity. Delegating _publishes_events avoids duplicate inference events. Confirm exception/interleaving ownership and binding in A.
